pages.title: 2025 Hyundai Santa Fe All Keys Lost in Cumming, GA
pages.summary: No key left for a 2025 Hyundai Santa Fe Hybrid. A genuine Hyundai smart key, matched by VIN, programmed at the car in Cumming.
pages.result_short: Genuine Hyundai smart key, matched by VIN
pages.problem: The owners had no key at all for their 2025 Hyundai Santa Fe Hybrid. It was the same family whose Silverado keys were lost in a house fire. A new Santa Fe needs a smart key with the exact part number for its VIN.
did: Checked the exact smart key part number for this Santa Fe by its VIN.
On the first visit, programmed a temporary key so the car could be driven: buttons and push-button start, without keyless entry.
Ordered a genuine Hyundai smart key with that part number.
Came back when it arrived and programmed the genuine key at the car in Cumming.
Tested lock and unlock, keyless entry and push-button start.
pages.result: The Santa Fe has a genuine Hyundai smart key again, with keyless entry and push-button start. All of it was done at the car, without the dealer.
pages.tip: On new Hyundai and Kia models the key has to match the exact part number for your VIN, not just the look. When every key is lost, a temporary key can get the car moving while the genuine one is on order.
pages.alt: Genuine Hyundai smart key held in front of the Santa Fe steering wheel, dash showing Ready
pages.tip_title: A tip for Hyundai and Kia owners

pages.title: 2008 Infiniti G35 Spare Smart Key in Sugar Hill, GA
pages.summary: A 2008 Infiniti G35 that sat parked for years had lost every key from its memory. We programmed a smart key at the car in Sugar Hill, almost an all keys lost job. No dealer trip.
pages.result_short: Spare smart key programmed on site
pages.problem: This 2008 Infiniti G35 had been sitting in a parking spot for years and was covered in a thick layer of dust. After the long sit and a dead battery, the car no longer recognized its original smart key. When we connected the programmer, the system showed 0 keys stored: every key had been wiped.
did: Came to the car in Sugar Hill.
Connected the programmer and read the key memory: 0 keys stored.
Ran what was almost an all keys lost procedure, since the car did not see the original key.
Programmed a new smart key and checked that the car starts with it by push-button start.
pages.result: The G35 starts again with a working smart key, made at the car with no trip to the dealer.
pages.tip: If a car sits for a long time, keep the battery on a maintainer or disconnect it. A fully drained battery can make some cars lose their stored keys, and then even the original key will not start the car.
pages.alt: New Infiniti smart key held in front of the G35 steering wheel
pages.tip_title: A tip if your car sits for months

pages.title: 2015 Nissan Altima Smart Key Programming in Lawrenceville, GA
pages.summary: A 2015 Nissan Altima stopped accepting its smart key even though the fob was alive. A new smart key was programmed at the car in Lawrenceville.
pages.result_short: New smart key programmed, car starts
pages.problem: The owner's smart key for a 2015 Nissan Altima looked fine: the battery was good and the chip inside read normally. But the car would no longer register it, so the push-to-start did not work with that fob.
did: Came to the car in Lawrenceville and tested the owner's fob first: the chip was alive, the car simply refused it.
Programmed a new smart key to the Altima on site.
Checked push-to-start, lock and unlock with the new key.
pages.result: The Altima starts and locks with the new smart key.
pages.tip: The dash on this car also showed an "I-Key System Error". On this job that message came from a fault code (B2604) that points to the park/neutral position switch, not to the key. A new key does not clear it, so it is worth reading the codes before buying a fob.
pages.alt: New smart key for a 2015 Nissan Altima held in front of the steering wheel

pages.title: 2019 Ford Ranger All Keys Lost in Johns Creek, GA
pages.summary: No keys at all for a 2019 Ford Ranger. The door lock was decoded, two high-security flip keys were cut in the driveway in Johns Creek and both were programmed to the truck.
pages.result_short: Two new high-security keys cut and programmed
pages.problem: The owner of a 2019 Ford Ranger in Johns Creek had lost every key. The Ranger uses a laser-cut high-security blade (HU101), which cannot be copied by eye, and there was no key to copy anyway.
did: Decoded the driver door lock with a Lishi pick-decoder to get the key code.
Cut two new flip keys on the mobile cutting machine, right in the driveway.
Programmed both keys to the truck and checked the door, the ignition and the remote buttons.
pages.result: The Ranger went from zero keys to two working keys, with no tow and no dealer visit.
pages.tip: On high-security Ford keys every cut matters. If a new key turns the ignition but not the door, one cut was read between two depths; re-checking that position fixes it.
pages.alt: Two new flip keys for a 2019 Ford Ranger in front of the steering wheel
pages.tip_title: A tip on high-security Ford keys
